name: Chapda Chutney
description: A tribal chutney of red weaver ants and their eggs collected from leaf nests in sal trees, ground with salt, chilli, garlic, ginger and coriander. It is tangy and fiery and is believed locally to boost immunity.
how_to_eat: Eat a small amount with rice or maize porridge to balance the heat.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chapda chutney' at Bastar weekly haats or tribal food festivals.

name: Fara
description: Steamed rice-flour dumplings, sometimes cut into small rolls or stuffed with spiced dal or vegetables, with minimal spice and coriander. Often called a desi momo, it is commonly made from leftover rice mixed with rice flour and tempered with mustard, cumin and curry leaves.
how_to_eat: Eat it warm with green or coconut chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for 'fara' or 'farra' at a local breakfast stall or home-style eatery.

name: Chila
description: A thin, dosa-like pancake of rice batter, often with urad dal, eaten at breakfast or as a snack. It is served with tomato, chilli and coriander chutney, and on Hareli it is traditionally cooked on sal leaves over an earthen griddle.
how_to_eat: Eat it hot with green or tomato chutney.
how_to_order: Ask for 'chila' (also spelt cheela) at a home-style breakfast stall.

name: Bafauri
description: Steamed dumplings of chana dal (or gram flour) with vegetables and spices, sometimes tossed in mustard oil. A healthier, unfried alternative to pakoras from the central plains.
how_to_eat: Eat them warm with chutney and tea.
how_to_order: Ask for 'bafauri' at a local snack or breakfast stall.

name: Aamat
description: A mixed-vegetable stew compared to sambar, flavoured with ginger-garlic paste, tamarind and spices and sometimes fermented rice water. In Bastar it is traditionally cooked with bamboo shoots, which add aroma.
how_to_order: Ask for 'aamat' at a Bastar or Chhattisgarhi home-style eatery.

name: Angakar Roti
description: A thick flatbread of coarse rice flour or jowar, cooked on a griddle or over burning charcoal, which gives it its name (angar means burning charcoal). It is traditionally eaten with badi chutney.
how_to_eat: Tear it and eat it with badi chutney or a curry.
how_to_order: Ask for 'angakar roti' at a Chhattisgarhi thali restaurant.

name: Bore Baasi
description: Cooked rice soaked overnight in water, curd or buttermilk and eaten the next day with pickle and raw onion. It is a summer meal believed to keep the body cool and hydrated, and reflects the local habit of not wasting rice.
how_to_eat: Eat it cold, with salt, raw onion and pickle on the side.

name: Muthia
description: Rice-flour dough with sesame seeds, onion, coriander and spices, shaped by hand and steamed rather than fried. It is a filling breakfast snack popular with rural farmers.
how_to_order: Ask for 'muthia' at a local breakfast stall.

name: Anarsa
description: Rice-flour discs studded with sesame, made for rituals and fairs.
how_to_eat: Eat it as a festival sweet.
